summary: The flag-window repeat executed as receipt 8502c21215334cbc81e6b277849a7d1d (exit 0, both subtests passed) and I folded it into the transfer account. Its single case again read the leader's transfer flag false before the call, returned an empty transfer error in 0 ms, and never installed the named demoted member; the retry case repeated that with the flag clear before its first attempt, six leaderless samples over 283, and leadership on a voter the caller did not name. All three transfer harnesses now hold two runs of the same request, so the account no longer rests on a single run for the flag probe. The repeat also exposed that my earlier reading of the 0 ms nil was too strong: the future is answered nil on the leader-loop path that closes when the leader leaves office, while the in-progress flag is set and reset on the leader-loop goroutine, with the source itself noting the window where a caller can see the request in flight after its future has been answered. A flag sample right after the call and the harness's 10 ms state sampler can therefore each miss a stepdown, a reset, or a same-node re-election, which is exactly what the two runs' differing final leader shows: the first ended on a different voter, the second on the same voter with zero leaderless samples. I replaced the counterevidence sentence that treated the clean first call as evidence the transfer did not run, rewrote the three-harness limitation as two runs per harness with the sampler caveat, extended the joint history, and kept all eight counterevidence items and six limitations. The conclusion stays violated with the scoped defect asserted, and the knowledge premises are unchanged, so both entries stay at revision 10. The repeat is cited in the account text and joint history rather than added to the recorded execution set, which belongs to the interpretation's own experiment identifier.
